newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt airport opens 120mln mark cargo terminal.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt airport opens 120mln mark cargo terminal.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said its new 120 million mark cargo terminal at Frankfurt airport's Cargo City South would go into operation on May 5.

The terminal, with a 44,000 square metre handling hall and two office blocks offering 10,000 square metres of office space, was officially opened in a ceremony attended by up to 5,000 guests on April 26.

In a welcome speech, FAG chairman Wilhelm Bender said the cargo terminal was the centre of the new one billion mark Cargo City South freight complex on the former U.S. military air base at Frankfurt airport.
The FAG cargo terminal building, constructed in little more than a year, showed that the airport wanted to stay the largest cargo airport in Europe, he stressed.
"Cargo City South is a clear signal to the market: With a total investment of more than one billion marks, we want to stay number one," he said.
Lufthansa Cargo AG had also gained more space for airfreight handling in its own Frankfurt cargo terminal as a result of the FAG switch to the south side of the airport, Bender noted.
FAG deputy chairman Manfred Schoelch, responsible for freight activities, said Cargo City South offered clients sufficient capacity, tailor-made services and quality at market-orientated prices.
The pylon-supported hall architecture of the FAG cargo terminal gave maximum cargo handling space, he added.

In a speech, Frankfurt mayor Petra Roth said the Far East was the most interesting growth region both for passenger and cargo traffic and the city of Frankfurt and the airport were engaged in joint marketing activities to tap this market.
Frankfurt had the largest Korean community in Europe with numerous companies setting up operations in the region, she noted.
